jobs.description:
German Voice AI Evaluator (Healthcare Front Desk Conversations)

About The Role

What if your native German fluency could help teach AI how to handle a real phone call to a doctor's office? We're looking for native German speakers based in the New York area to hold natural spoken conversations with an AI healthcare receptionist, then evaluate how well it listens, responds, and takes action.

New York's large German-speaking community — from recent expats to heritage speakers — makes it an ideal place to find people with the authentic, natural German speech this project demands. You'll role-play as a patient using fictional personas we provide, record short conversations, and grade the AI's performance.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role for people with clear German speech, strong attention to detail, and an ear for what sounds natural and fluent.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Contract (task-based)
Location: Remote
Commitment: Flexible, work at your own pace

What You'll Do

Hold 4 to 5 minute spoken conversations in German with an AI front desk assistant, playing a fictional patient
Say natural trigger phrases to test whether the AI makes the correct function calls — for example, checking a patient record, booking an appointment, or verifying insurance
Review transcripts and classify how accurately the AI understood you and responded
Flag issues such as mispronunciations, cutoffs, interruptions, delays, and incorrect function calls, including timestamps
Test how the AI handles background noise, short replies such as "ja," "nein," or "okay," long numbers, emotional moments, and sensitive or unsafe requests
Follow detailed labeling guidelines consistently and submit high-quality work

Who You Are

Native or near-native German speaker with a clear, natural speaking voice
Detail-oriented, with the patience to review recordings and transcripts closely
Comfortable role-playing a patient and sounding authentic in conversation
Able to follow multi-step instructions and apply them consistently
Reliable and self-directed when working independently
Access to a quiet space, a good microphone, a stable internet connection, and a second device for playing background noise
Comfortable using web-based tools

Nice to Have

Experience in voice AI evaluation, data annotation, or QA testing
Background in healthcare administration, customer service, or call centre work
Familiarity with spoken German variants from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland
Linguistics or language-focused academic background
Familiarity with medical terminology in German

Why Join Us

Work on cutting-edge AI projects alongside leading research labs
Fully remote and flexible — work when and where it suits you
Task-based work with real autonomy
Directly help make voice AI more accurate, natural, and safe in healthcare settings
Potential for ongoing work as new projects launch

JOB TITLE: Engineering Specialist

LOCATION: San Francisco or Sacramento

JOB OPENING #: 6780

OVERVIEW 

The Judicial Council of California is accepting applications for the position of Engineering Specialist (Energy & Sustainability) with the Facilities Services office.

The Engineering Specialist will be responsible for analyzing and validating utility data, including electricity, natural gas, water, waste, and fuels, for courthouses in the assigned regions in Central and Southern California. The role supports sustainability-focused decision-making by identifying usage trends, verifying billing accuracy, and flagging inefficiencies. A significant focus is on maintaining high-quality data in platforms such as ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and the Energy Management Information System (EMIS) to support energy reduction, water conservation, and decarbonization goals.

The Engineering Specialist supports the monthly and annual reporting of energy and water use, costs, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, as well as regulatory compliance reporting, including GHG inventory data compilation and support for Assembly Bill (AB) 802 benchmarking. Trend analysis to identify peak demand, abnormal water use, and inefficiencies is a key aspect of this work.

This position also involves conducting or supporting energy and water audits, life cycle cost analysis, and technical reviews of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems in support of energy efficiency, water efficiency, and waste reduction upgrades and capital project planning. The Engineering Specialist helps identify and track utility incentives and rebates, recommends energy- and water-efficient equipment, and contributes to the development of energy, water conservation, and waste reduction policy. The position serves as the technical water and waste resource for the Sustainability Unit and provides related educational training for the field staff and court staff.

The Judicial Council 

The Judicial Council of California is the policy setting body for the state court system and has constitutionally conferred statewide rule-making authority. This authority includes developing, advocating for, and allocating the judicial branch budget. A majority of Council members are California state justices and judges; however, the Council also includes lawyers, legislators, and court administrators.

By enhancing its role as a leadership, knowledge, and service resource for the judicial branch, the Judicial Council’s staff organization seeks to continue to evolve as one of California’s most dynamic public service entities, focused on improving access to justice for all Californians by innovating and responding to the changing needs of the courts and the public. As a government body charged with improving the statewide administration of justice, the Judicial Council has multiple offices with diverse responsibilities relating to court policy and operations. As employees of the council, every member of staff should view and approach their work as one Judicial Council with a public service mission that is greater than the sum of its parts.

The Judicial Council strives for work-life balance, including substantial vacation and holiday time. In addition, we offer an excellent benefits package, including pension, medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible spending, up to $130 per month reimbursement for qualifying commuting costs, student loan forgiveness as part of Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), and retirement savings plans. In San Francisco, the office is only a 7-minute walk from the Civic Center BART station. In Sacramento, the office is minutes from downtown, just north of Discovery Park.

The Judicial Council offers hybrid work arrangements for many positions. The successful candidate will be expected to work in person at the Judicial Council’s San Francisco or Sacramento office at least two days per week, based on their office leader’s direction, and reside in the areas surrounding these locations. To be eligible for Judicial Council employment and participation in the Judicial Council’s Hybrid Work Program, a prospective or current employee’s primary residence/remote work location must be in the State of California and within a 150-mile driving radius of their assigned reporting location.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Review and validate utility bills for electricity, natural gas, water, waste, and fuels for courthouses in the assigned regions, including daily batch reviews, late bill monitoring, and accurate entry of paper and electronic invoices in the EMIS.
• Monitor utility data quality across the portfolio in the EMIS and ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, identify discrepancies, and coordinate corrections with utility vendors, Branch Accounting, Procurement, and other internal stakeholders.
• Serve as the utility vendor liaison for the assigned regions, resolving billing discrepancies, service concerns, payment issues, and account setup for new and transferred facilities.
• Benchmark energy, water, and waste performance across the Judicial Council's portfolio of over 400 facilities (use, energy use intensity, cost, and GHG emissions), and perform trend analysis to identify demand peaks, leaks, abnormal use, and operational inefficiencies.
• Coordinate and review energy, water, and waste audits and retro-commissioning studies, and prepare project recommendations with estimated costs, savings, simple payback, life cycle cost analysis, and available utility incentives.
• Develop and maintain energy and sustainability dashboards and monthly energy and water reports for internal and external stakeholders.
• Serve as the technical resource for Facilities Services on water efficiency and waste reduction, including plumbing fixtures, irrigation controls, water metering, leak detection, and recycling and composting programs, and contribute to related policies and technical standards.
• Support renewable energy, battery storage, EV charging, and capital project work, including utility incentive applications, energy model reviews, and analysis of financing options.
• Compile annual GHG inventory data, including refrigerant, diesel, fleet fuel, and staff travel data, and support AB 802 benchmarking and other regulatory reporting.
• Provide training to Facility Management field staff, service providers, and court staff on energy and water conservation, utility incentive programs, and Title 24 energy code updates.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree, preferably in a directly related field that would provide the knowledge and skills necessary for technical facility and construction engineering. An additional four (4) years of professional experience as noted above may substitute for the bachelor’s degree. Or, additional directly related experience and/or education may be substituted on a year-for-year basis.

DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience reviewing, validating, or processing utility bills and maintaining utility account data for a multi-site portfolio.
• Experience with ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and an energy management information system or utility bill management platform.
• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with a data visualization tool such as Power BI.
• Knowledge of building systems, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning, lighting and controls, plumbing, and irrigation, and of energy and water auditing.
• Experience with life cycle cost analysis and utility incentive programs, such as California Energy Design Assistance, custom incentives, and on-bill financing.
• Knowledge of GHG inventory protocols, such as The Climate Registry and California Air Resources Board methods, and of California building benchmarking requirements under AB 802.
• Knowledge of waste reduction, recycling, and composting programs, and of water conservation strategies.
• Professional Engineer license, Certified Energy Manager certification, LEED Accredited Professional credential, or similar.

LICENSING AND CERTIFICATIONS

Valid driver’s license.

OTHER

About The Role

Our client is looking for experienced scientists and engineers to evaluate how frontier AI models handle real technical work: analyzing test, measurement or process data, sizing and verifying a design, designing an experiment and reading it out, interpreting a simulation, writing the technical report. You bring the judgment you have built catching the unit error in a test file, the multiple comparisons trap in a process improvement study, and the assumption that does not hold at the boundary. We bring the model output that judgment is needed to grade.

In this role, you will design challenging, realistic tasks drawn from your own practice, such as a calculation package with stated assumptions and checks, a test plan and data analysis, a failure or deviation investigation, a design trade study, an experimental protocol with acceptance criteria, a circuit or system design review, or a technical report, run them through frontier AI agents, and evaluate what comes back against a professional standard.

Across our STEM and Data Science programs, tasks are grounded in real day-to-day workflows and checked against frontier models so only genuinely hard tasks make it through. Some projects are authored and verified in code, so coding / scientific computing is a strong plus and is required on those projects.

You will work with realistic professional files, the kind a practitioner in your field actually handles, which you assemble yourself. Some tasks are compact, built around a handful of files; others are larger scenarios that take several days to build. In every case the goal is the same: a task a competent professional in your field would complete correctly and a frontier model currently gets wrong.

This is not a traditional science or engineering role. You will be helping build better AI by putting your knowledge to work in a structured, flexible, fully remote environment. The work is long-form and self-directed, and clear written reasoning matters as much as technical depth.

Responsibilities

Design challenging, realistic technical tasks drawn from your own day-to-day work: the scenario, a prompt phrased the way you would brief a trusted colleague, and the supporting files an engineer or scientist would need (test data, drawings or schematics, specifications, simulation outputs, lab records, reports), which you author yourself.
Run those tasks through frontier AI models and evaluate the deliverable they produce (the calculation, analysis, design review or report) against the standard you would hold a colleague to.
Compare two model outputs on identical prompts and files, decide which performed better, and document where each fell short.
Write detailed grading rubrics that specify what a correct deliverable must contain (the right assumptions stated, the right method, the right magnitudes and units, the right failure modes considered), and explain in writing why a response passes or fails each one.
Flag concrete failures with evidence: unit and scaling errors, misread data, unsupported conclusions, fabricated or ignored source files, missed safety or boundary conditions, and off-brief interpretation of the ask.
Contribute across your discipline and adjacent ones, and review and refine tasks built by other experts.

Qualifications

2+ years of applied experience preferred in one of the core sciences (mathematics, physics, chemistry, or biology) or in an engineering discipline (electrical and electronics, civil and structural, materials, chemical and process, environmental and earth sciences, or similar) or in data science.
In progress Bachelor’s degree or higher. We prefer 2+ years of experience outside undergraduate study.
Coding / scientific computing is a strong plus and is required on some projects: comfortable writing and verifying work in code (Python or similar) and working at the command line.
Hands-on with real data and the tools of your field: instrument and test data, measurement files, simulation outputs, schematics or drawings, and the analysis tools that go with them (MATLAB, Python or R; SPICE and PCB tools; FEA or CFD; GIS; chromatography or spectroscopy software).
Comfort with statistical and experimental reasoning: experiment design, measurement error and uncertainty, and the common statistical traps. The assessment leans on this.
Working understanding of adjacent sub-disciplines, enough to assess work outside your own specialty and point out what was done correctly or incorrectly.
Hands-on practitioner: you currently do (or recently did) the work yourself at an individual-contributor level, not solely in a managerial capacity.
Full professional or native-level written and spoken English; you can articulate why a result is wrong, not only that it is.
General familiarity with AI and LLM tools: you can tell a well-reasoned answer from a plausible-sounding but incorrect one.
Baseline tech literacy: comfortable with cloud file tools (e.g., Google Workspace), managing browser profiles, downloading and installing desktop apps (e.g., Claude), and everyday file handling (e.g., converting between Excel and Google Sheets, zipping files for sharing).
Advanced degree or professional licensure (PE, chartered status) is a plus but not required. Practical applied work outweighs credentials.

JOB TITLE: Engineering Specialist

LOCATION: San Francisco or Sacramento

JOB OPENING #: 6780

OVERVIEW 

The Judicial Council of California is accepting applications for the position of Engineering Specialist (Energy & Sustainability) with the Facilities Services office.

The Engineering Specialist will be responsible for analyzing and validating utility data, including electricity, natural gas, water, waste, and fuels, for courthouses in the assigned regions in Central and Southern California. The role supports sustainability-focused decision-making by identifying usage trends, verifying billing accuracy, and flagging inefficiencies. A significant focus is on maintaining high-quality data in platforms such as ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and the Energy Management Information System (EMIS) to support energy reduction, water conservation, and decarbonization goals.

The Engineering Specialist supports the monthly and annual reporting of energy and water use, costs, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, as well as regulatory compliance reporting, including GHG inventory data compilation and support for Assembly Bill (AB) 802 benchmarking. Trend analysis to identify peak demand, abnormal water use, and inefficiencies is a key aspect of this work.

This position also involves conducting or supporting energy and water audits, life cycle cost analysis, and technical reviews of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems in support of energy efficiency, water efficiency, and waste reduction upgrades and capital project planning. The Engineering Specialist helps identify and track utility incentives and rebates, recommends energy- and water-efficient equipment, and contributes to the development of energy, water conservation, and waste reduction policy. The position serves as the technical water and waste resource for the Sustainability Unit and provides related educational training for the field staff and court staff.

The Judicial Council 

The Judicial Council of California is the policy setting body for the state court system and has constitutionally conferred statewide rule-making authority. This authority includes developing, advocating for, and allocating the judicial branch budget. A majority of Council members are California state justices and judges; however, the Council also includes lawyers, legislators, and court administrators.

By enhancing its role as a leadership, knowledge, and service resource for the judicial branch, the Judicial Council’s staff organization seeks to continue to evolve as one of California’s most dynamic public service entities, focused on improving access to justice for all Californians by innovating and responding to the changing needs of the courts and the public. As a government body charged with improving the statewide administration of justice, the Judicial Council has multiple offices with diverse responsibilities relating to court policy and operations. As employees of the council, every member of staff should view and approach their work as one Judicial Council with a public service mission that is greater than the sum of its parts.

The Judicial Council strives for work-life balance, including substantial vacation and holiday time. In addition, we offer an excellent benefits package, including pension, medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible spending, up to $130 per month reimbursement for qualifying commuting costs, student loan forgiveness as part of Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), and retirement savings plans. In San Francisco, the office is only a 7-minute walk from the Civic Center BART station. In Sacramento, the office is minutes from downtown, just north of Discovery Park.

The Judicial Council offers hybrid work arrangements for many positions. The successful candidate will be expected to work in person at the Judicial Council’s San Francisco or Sacramento office at least two days per week, based on their office leader’s direction, and reside in the areas surrounding these locations. To be eligible for Judicial Council employment and participation in the Judicial Council’s Hybrid Work Program, a prospective or current employee’s primary residence/remote work location must be in the State of California and within a 150-mile driving radius of their assigned reporting location.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Review and validate utility bills for electricity, natural gas, water, waste, and fuels for courthouses in the assigned regions, including daily batch reviews, late bill monitoring, and accurate entry of paper and electronic invoices in the EMIS.

• Serve as the utility vendor liaison for the assigned regions, resolving billing discrepancies, service concerns, payment issues, and account setup for new and transferred facilities.

• Coordinate and review energy, water, and waste audits and retro-commissioning studies, and prepare project recommendations with estimated costs, savings, simple payback, life cycle cost analysis, and available utility incentives.
• Develop and maintain energy and sustainability dashboards and monthly energy and water reports for internal and external stakeholders.
• Serve as the technical resource for Facilities Services on water efficiency and waste reduction, including plumbing fixtures, irrigation controls, water metering, leak detection, and recycling and composting programs, and contribute to related policies and technical standards.
• Support renewable energy, battery storage, EV charging, and capital project work, including utility incentive applications, energy model reviews, and analysis of financing options.
• Compile annual GHG inventory data, including refrigerant, diesel, fleet fuel, and staff travel data, and support AB 802 benchmarking and other regulatory reporting.
• Provide training to Facility Management field staff, service providers, and court staff on energy and water conservation, utility incentive programs, and Title 24 energy code updates.

Bachelor’s degree, preferably in a directly related field that would provide the knowledge and skills necessary for technical facility and construction engineering. An additional four (4) years of professional experience as noted above may substitute for the bachelor’s degree. Or, additional directly related experience and/or education may be substituted on a year-for-year basis.

About The Role

Our client is looking for experienced scientists and engineers to evaluate how frontier AI models handle real technical work: analyzing test, measurement or process data, sizing and verifying a design, designing an experiment and reading it out, interpreting a simulation, writing the technical report. You bring the judgment you have built catching the unit error in a test file, the multiple comparisons trap in a process improvement study, and the assumption that does not hold at the boundary. We bring the model output that judgment is needed to grade.

In this role, you will design challenging, realistic tasks drawn from your own practice, such as a calculation package with stated assumptions and checks, a test plan and data analysis, a failure or deviation investigation, a design trade study, an experimental protocol with acceptance criteria, a circuit or system design review, or a technical report, run them through frontier AI agents, and evaluate what comes back against a professional standard.

Across our STEM and Data Science programs, tasks are grounded in real day-to-day workflows and checked against frontier models so only genuinely hard tasks make it through. Some projects are authored and verified in code, so coding / scientific computing is a strong plus and is required on those projects.

You will work with realistic professional files, the kind a practitioner in your field actually handles, which you assemble yourself. Some tasks are compact, built around a handful of files; others are larger scenarios that take several days to build. In every case the goal is the same: a task a competent professional in your field would complete correctly and a frontier model currently gets wrong.

This is not a traditional science or engineering role. You will be helping build better AI by putting your knowledge to work in a structured, flexible, fully remote environment. The work is long-form and self-directed, and clear written reasoning matters as much as technical depth.

Responsibilities

Design challenging, realistic technical tasks drawn from your own day-to-day work: the scenario, a prompt phrased the way you would brief a trusted colleague, and the supporting files an engineer or scientist would need (test data, drawings or schematics, specifications, simulation outputs, lab records, reports), which you author yourself.
Run those tasks through frontier AI models and evaluate the deliverable they produce (the calculation, analysis, design review or report) against the standard you would hold a colleague to.
Compare two model outputs on identical prompts and files, decide which performed better, and document where each fell short.
Write detailed grading rubrics that specify what a correct deliverable must contain (the right assumptions stated, the right method, the right magnitudes and units, the right failure modes considered), and explain in writing why a response passes or fails each one.
Flag concrete failures with evidence: unit and scaling errors, misread data, unsupported conclusions, fabricated or ignored source files, missed safety or boundary conditions, and off-brief interpretation of the ask.
Contribute across your discipline and adjacent ones, and review and refine tasks built by other experts.

Qualifications

2+ years of applied experience preferred in one of the core sciences (mathematics, physics, chemistry, or biology) or in an engineering discipline (electrical and electronics, civil and structural, materials, chemical and process, environmental and earth sciences, or similar) or in data science.
In progress Bachelor’s degree or higher. We prefer 2+ years of experience outside undergraduate study.
Coding / scientific computing is a strong plus and is required on some projects: comfortable writing and verifying work in code (Python or similar) and working at the command line.
Hands-on with real data and the tools of your field: instrument and test data, measurement files, simulation outputs, schematics or drawings, and the analysis tools that go with them (MATLAB, Python or R; SPICE and PCB tools; FEA or CFD; GIS; chromatography or spectroscopy software).
Comfort with statistical and experimental reasoning: experiment design, measurement error and uncertainty, and the common statistical traps. The assessment leans on this.
Working understanding of adjacent sub-disciplines, enough to assess work outside your own specialty and point out what was done correctly or incorrectly.
Hands-on practitioner: you currently do (or recently did) the work yourself at an individual-contributor level, not solely in a managerial capacity.
Full professional or native-level written and spoken English; you can articulate why a result is wrong, not only that it is.
General familiarity with AI and LLM tools: you can tell a well-reasoned answer from a plausible-sounding but incorrect one.
Baseline tech literacy: comfortable with cloud file tools (e.g., Google Workspace), managing browser profiles, downloading and installing desktop apps (e.g., Claude), and everyday file handling (e.g., converting between Excel and Google Sheets, zipping files for sharing).
Advanced degree or professional licensure (PE, chartered status) is a plus but not required. Practical applied work outweighs credentials.

Overview Of The Position

The Engineering Specialist will be a key Subject Matter Expert supporting the production department's Integrated Team, and the Product Support Engineering Group as needed. This role will have demonstrated reliability, capacity, and effective working knowledge of the following PHSMWA TTE program / Product Support responsibilities and will accurately resolve TTE and technical matters to meet the operational and compliance priorities of Production, Engineering, QA, and most importantly, the customer. The Engineering Specialist has the responsibility and authority to perform assigned tasks.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Ensure tooling and calibrated items are appropriately labeled, organized, stored, and accessible in the department. Find lost tooling; prevent duplicates and waste
Ensure broken or poorly performing tooling is remedied in a timely manner, before it becomes an emergency or a production delay
Generate TTE requisitions with the right information to ensure special tooling and equipment is defined, made (or purchased), and identified successfully
Write, substantiate, validate TTE Equivalencies. Initiate and update unit ETMLs and Test Data Sheets.
Assist with evaluating New Capabilities for technical complexity, fit to existing, potential TTE costs to add.
Train production technicians on usage of TTE, Test Stands, or other technical processes as needed

Assist with Corrective Action Requirements as necessary
